address: Cô Giang Street, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
w: An 80-year-old cháo lòng (pork-offal congee) gánh that started at Cầu Muối market and still cooks its silky congee in a hand-welded pot made from two aluminium basins turned mouth-to-mouth. Three generations in; Bà Út alone has ladled it for over 60 years, and the menu has never changed.

address: Hai Bà Trưng Street (near hẻm 191), District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
w: A more-than-70-year-old northern-style bánh mì tray (mẹt) sold from the pavement, its loaves stacked on a woven tray the way Cụ Lý carried them from the North in the 1950s. Named a Top 10 long-running (50+ year) bánh mì brand by the Vietnam Record Organization in 2023; sells hundreds of loaves each morning.

address: 19 Nguyễn Huy Tự, Đa Kao Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
w: An ice-cream shop open since 1958, whose founder Cụ Lý Thân learned the craft in Cambodia before setting up in Đa Kao; now run by the third/fourth generation on a near-70-year recipe. Its tube ice cream (kem ống) and kem ký are churned from condensed milk, coconut, beans, sweet potato and fresh fruit — a genuine 1950s Saigon taste that has found a new gen-Z following.

n: Bánh Canh Cua 194 Võ Văn Tần
address: 194 Võ Văn Tần (đầu hẻm), District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
w: A bánh canh cua (crab tapioca-noodle soup) counter at the mouth of alley 194 that Võ Kim Hồng's grandmother started in the early 1980s — over 40 years and now into the fourth generation. Its signature is bánh canh cua xào, stir-fried freshly-molted crab from a long-time Bến Thành supplier.

address: 50 Hồ Biểu Chánh, Ward 12, Phú Nhuận District, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
w: A three-generation Hanoi-style bún thang house, its clear-sweet broth simmered from chicken bones and dried shrimp and topped with the dish's fine julienne of egg, chicken and giò. A long-loved pocket of northern refinement in Phú Nhuận, now run by third-generation owner Bích Ngọc.
dish: bún thang (Hanoi layered chicken noodle soup)

address: Lô I chung cư Ngô Gia Tự, Ward 2, District 10, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
w: A pork-offal congee stall opened in 1977 under the Ngô Gia Tự apartments, its garlic-fragrant, smooth cháo and sweet giò chìa unchanged across 45+ years and two generations. Nicknamed 'cháo bụi' by comedian Việt Hương, a regular from before she was famous.

address: Chợ Lớn, District 5, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
w: A Chinese-Vietnamese bánh mì brand in Chợ Lớn established in 1968, distinguished by its roasted pâté and a strongly Cantonese-flavoured xíu mại (siu mai) that sets it apart from central or northern versions. Named a Top 10 long-running (50+ year) bánh mì brand by the Vietnam Record Organization.
dish: bánh mì xíu mại (Cantonese-style pork-meatball sandwich)

address: 11A Cao Thắng, Ward 2, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
w: A northern-style bánh cuốn shop of more than half a century on a two-metre-wide Cao Thắng storefront, where — however crowded — the cook still hand-pours each rice-and-tapioca crêpe to order rather than using a machine. A quiet multi-generation Saigon fixture.

address: Thuận Kiều Street, Ward 4, District 11, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
w: The oldest cơm tấm (broken-rice) brand in Saigon, born on Thuận Kiều Street in Chợ Lớn before 1975 and named for it. A pioneer that broadened cơm tấm beyond the classic sườn-bì-chả with dishes like grilled chicken and cá lóc kho, it has anchored District 11 for generations.

n: Bún Bò Dồi Chiên Cô Minh
address: Phan Xích Long, Phú Nhuận District, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
w: A bún bò counter open since 1984 whose one-of-a-kind twist is dồi chiên — fried blood-and-herb sausage — dropped into the bowl, a recipe unchanged for nearly four decades and passed down from the owner's elder sister. Around 300 bowls a day; the stall has moved several times but only grown.
dish: bún bò dồi chiên (beef noodle soup with fried sausage)

address: 166 Phó Cơ Điều (chợ Thiếc), Ward 6, District 11, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
w: A pavement súp cua (crab soup) stall by chợ Thiếc that has drawn packed evening crowds for over 20 years, ladling out around 10 pots a day thick with crab, quail egg, pig brain and marrow. A cheap, beloved chợ-Thiếc institution profiled repeatedly in the local press.

n: Bún Riêu Cua Ốc Thanh Hải
address: 14/12 Kỳ Đồng, District 3, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
w: A northern-style bún ốc riêu cua tucked in an alley off Kỳ Đồng since 1982, cooked by Thái Bình-born Phạm Thị Hải, who keeps the field-crab-and-snail broth exactly as her family ate it back home. Over 40 years of a homesick Bắc flavour rarely found in the South.
dish: bún ốc riêu cua (northern snail & crab noodle soup)

n: Gỏi Khô Bò Công Viên Lê Văn Tám
address: Hai Bà Trưng Street (opposite Lê Văn Tám Park), District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
w: A near-50-year gỏi khô bò (green-papaya salad with dried beef) stall on the pavement facing Lê Văn Tám Park — a sub-1-metre table and a glass case that has become a Saigon street-food legend. Crisp shredded papaya, chewy dried beef and a sweet-sour-spicy sauce; foreign visitors now queue and eat sitting on the kerb.

address: 9 Huỳnh Khương Ninh, Đa Kao Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
w: A more-than-60-year bánh mì shop named for its founder — the seventh child, Quang — famous for a pâté that regulars swear by and a flavour they say has never changed. It began at the Đinh Tiên Hoàng corner before settling on Huỳnh Khương Ninh.

address: 43 Tôn Thất Đạm, Nguyễn Thái Bình Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
w: A 60–70-year hủ tiếu cá landmark on Tôn Thất Đạm, its wide, soft rice noodles and clear Cantonese-sweet broth crowned with wafer-thin slices of fish — a Hoa-Việt fusion that is a point of Saigon pride. So loved that singer Hari Won has been photographed waiting before it opens.

address: 318/1 Bùi Hữu Nghĩa, Ward 1, Bình Thạnh District, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
w: A famed evening xôi gà (chicken sticky-rice) gánh hidden behind a power pole near chợ Bà Chiểu, selling hundreds of packets a night despite having no seats. Chicken, Chinese sausage and offal versions, ladled by a stall that has become a Bình Thạnh ritual.

address: Corner of Trương Định & Nguyễn An Ninh, Bến Thành Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
w: A single-dish bún mọc house beside Bến Thành market, going since 1980 from a small gánh to a corner shop, its steaming bowl piled with sườn, mọc and four kinds of chả. The pork balls are hand-made from giò sống and wood-ear, the broth skimmed clear — over 40 years of northern flavour in the centre of town.

address: 12 Nguyễn Huy Tự, Đa Kao Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
w: A cháo lòng stall opposite Đa Kao market that Đa Kao locals have known since the 1960s — over 50 years and three generations. Its signature dồi is stuffed not with the usual blood and herbs but with marinated, fried pork tenderloin, which is why it sits among the priciest bowls in town.

n: Mì Vịt Tiềm Quảng Huê Viên
address: Corner of Phan Đình Phùng & Nguyễn Trọng Tuyển, Phú Nhuận District, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
w: One of Saigon's oldest Cantonese kitchens, traced by its owners to a 1940 congee shop and famous for 70+ years across three generations for mì vịt tiềm — herbal-stewed duck, its skin both chewy and crisp, over springy egg noodles. Small and not cheap, but a Hoa culinary heirloom.
dish: mì vịt tiềm (herbal stewed-duck egg noodles)

address: Hẻm 241 Bến Vân Đồn, Ward 2, District 4, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
w: A dawn cơm tấm hidden in an alley off Bến Vân Đồn, open from 4am and sold out by 9am, run for over 40 years by Cô Phượng and her daughters on the mother's marinades for sườn and pâté. A District 4 breakfast institution eaten in front of an old house.
dish: cơm tấm sườn (dawn broken-rice with grilled pork)
